 Focus on financial stability and sustainable growth of the Group
As announced by Rosenbauer International AG’s Supervisory Board in October 2025, Jörg Schuschnig has been appointed as the new Chief Financial Officer (CFO). He takes up his new role on April 1, 2026. Schuschnig succeeds CEO Robert Ottel, who had taken on the CFO agendas on an interim basis in addition to his work as Chief Executive Officer. The appointment is for a term of office of three years. 
“With Jörg Schuschnig, we are delighted to have acquired someone with profound financial expertise and many years of industry experience. The Executive Board team is now complete and in an excellent position to tackle the challenges of the years ahead. Our shared goal remains the successful further development of Rosenbauer as a global market leader in the firefighting industry,” said Christian Reisinger, Chairman of the Supervisory Board.
“I would like to thank the Supervisory Board for their confidence in me and look forward to working with my team and my colleagues on the Executive Board. Together, we will further strengthen Rosenbauer’s financial stability and harness the Group’s existing potential for further growth and increased earnings. I will focus in particular on consistently establishing efficient digital processes in the finance division, increasing efficiency, and further developing global governance within the company,” said CFO Jörg Schuschnig.
Schuschnig is a recognized financial expert with a doctorate in business administration and many years of international experience in various companies. He has been CFO of the Coveris Group since 2022. Previously, he was CEO and CFO of BGO Holding GmbH and CFO and COO of Bene GmbH. Before that, he spent around nine years with the Mondi Group, where he was an Executive Board member of the Industrial Bags and Consumer Flexibles business units. Earlier in his career, he held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group.

The Supervisory Board of Rosenbauer International AG today appointed Jörg Schuschnig as the new Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Rosenbauer International AG. He takes over this role from CEO Robert Ottel, who had been serving as interim CFO since the beginning of July. Jörg Schuschnig will take up his position on the Executive Board on October 1, 2026 at the latest. The appointment is for a period of three years.
Christian Reisinger, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Rosenbauer International AG: “We are very pleased to welcome Dr. Jörg Schuschnig, a seasoned financial expert with many years of industrial experience, to Rosenbauer International AG. With his appointment, our executive board is now complete and excellently positioned to tackle the challenges of the coming years. Our shared goal remains to successfully continue developing Rosenbauer as the global market leader in firefighting sector.”
Jörg Schuschnig, designated CFO of Rosenbauer International AG: “I am delighted to be taking on this new role at Rosenbauer – a company that, to me, stands for cutting-edge innovation, top-tier quality, and absolute reliability. Together with the team, I’m committed to further strengthening Rosenbauer’s financial stability and growth potential. A particular focus for me will be embedding efficiency and digital processes into our financial operations and advancing global governance to enhance our international competitiveness.”
As a recognized financial expert, Jörg Schuschnig brings many years of experience from various companies. Since 2022, he has served as CFO of Coveris Group. Prior to that, his career included roles as CEO and CFO of BGO Holding GmbH, as well as CFO and COO at Bene GmbH. He also spent over nine years at the Mondi Group, where he was a board member of the business units Industrial Bags and Consumer Flexibles. Earlier in his career, he held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group. Jörg Schuschnig studied Business Administration at WU Vienna and holds a doctorate.

Jörg Schuschnig appointed new CFO of Rosenbauer International AG

Rosenbauer International AG
by Mag. Tiemon Kiesenhofer
Business news for the stock market
Rosenbauer International AG: Jörg Schuschnig appointed new CFO of Rosenbauer International AG
Leonding (pta000/03.10.2025/09:45 UTC+2)
The Supervisory Board of Rosenbauer International AG today appointed Jörg Schuschnig as the new Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Rosenbauer International AG. He takes over this role from CEO Robert Ottel, who had been serving as interim CFO since the beginning of July. Jörg Schuschnig will take up his position on the Executive Board on October 1, 2026 at the latest. The appointment is for a period of three years.
Christian Reisinger, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Rosenbauer International AG: "We are very pleased to welcome Dr. Jörg Schuschnig, a seasoned financial expert with many years of industrial experience, to Rosenbauer International AG. With his appointment, our executive board is now complete and excellently positioned to tackle the challenges of the coming years. Our shared goal remains to successfully continue developing Rosenbauer as the global market leader in firefighting sector."
Jörg Schuschnig, designated CFO of Rosenbauer International AG: "I am delighted to be taking on this new role at Rosenbauer – a company that, to me, stands for cutting-edge innovation, top-tier quality, and absolute reliability. Together with the team, I'm committed to further strengthening Rosenbauer's financial stability and growth potential. A particular focus for me will be embedding efficiency and digital processes into our financial operations and advancing global governance to enhance our international competitiveness."
As a recognized financial expert, Jörg Schuschnig brings many years of experience from various companies. Since 2022, he has served as CFO of Coveris Group. Prior to that, his career included roles as CEO and CFO of BGO Holding GmbH, as well as CFO and COO at Bene GmbH. He also spent over nine years at the Mondi Group, where he was a board member of the business units Industrial Bags and Consumer Flexibles. Earlier in his career, he held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group. Jörg Schuschnig studied Business Administration at WU Vienna and holds a doctorate.

 Focus on financial stability and sustainable growth of the Group
As announced by Rosenbauer International AG’s Supervisory Board in October 2025, Jörg Schuschnig has been appointed as the new Chief Financial Officer (CFO). He takes up his new role on April 1, 2026. Schuschnig succeeds CEO Robert Ottel, who had taken on the CFO agendas on an interim basis in addition to his work as Chief Executive Officer. The appointment is for a term of office of three years. 
“With Jörg Schuschnig, we are delighted to have acquired someone with profound financial expertise and many years of industry experience. The Executive Board team is now complete and in an excellent position to tackle the challenges of the years ahead. Our shared goal remains the successful further development of Rosenbauer as a global market leader in the firefighting industry,” said Christian Reisinger, Chairman of the Supervisory Board.
“I would like to thank the Supervisory Board for their confidence in me and look forward to working with my team and my colleagues on the Executive Board. Together, we will further strengthen Rosenbauer’s financial stability and harness the Group’s existing potential for further growth and increased earnings. I will focus in particular on consistently establishing efficient digital processes in the finance division, increasing efficiency, and further developing global governance within the company,” said CFO Jörg Schuschnig.
Schuschnig is a recognized financial expert with a doctorate in business administration and many years of international experience in various companies. He has been CFO of the Coveris Group since 2022. Previously, he was CEO and CFO of BGO Holding GmbH and CFO and COO of Bene GmbH. Before that, he spent around nine years with the Mondi Group, where he was an Executive Board member of the Industrial Bags and Consumer Flexibles business units. Earlier in his career, he held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group.

The Supervisory Board of Rosenbauer International AG today appointed Jörg Schuschnig as the new Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Rosenbauer International AG. He takes over this role from CEO Robert Ottel, who had been serving as interim CFO since the beginning of July. Jörg Schuschnig will take up his position on the Executive Board on October 1, 2026 at the latest. The appointment is for a period of three years.
Christian Reisinger, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Rosenbauer International AG: “We are very pleased to welcome Dr. Jörg Schuschnig, a seasoned financial expert with many years of industrial experience, to Rosenbauer International AG. With his appointment, our executive board is now complete and excellently positioned to tackle the challenges of the coming years. Our shared goal remains to successfully continue developing Rosenbauer as the global market leader in firefighting sector.”
Jörg Schuschnig, designated CFO of Rosenbauer International AG: “I am delighted to be taking on this new role at Rosenbauer – a company that, to me, stands for cutting-edge innovation, top-tier quality, and absolute reliability. Together with the team, I’m committed to further strengthening Rosenbauer’s financial stability and growth potential. A particular focus for me will be embedding efficiency and digital processes into our financial operations and advancing global governance to enhance our international competitiveness.”
As a recognized financial expert, Jörg Schuschnig brings many years of experience from various companies. Since 2022, he has served as CFO of Coveris Group. Prior to that, his career included roles as CEO and CFO of BGO Holding GmbH, as well as CFO and COO at Bene GmbH. He also spent over nine years at the Mondi Group, where he was a board member of the business units Industrial Bags and Consumer Flexibles. Earlier in his career, he held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group. Jörg Schuschnig studied Business Administration at WU Vienna and holds a doctorate.

Rosenbauer appoints Jörg Schuschnig as Chief Financial Officer
Schuschnig to take up role by October 2026
Rosenbauer International AG has announced the appointment of Jörg Schuschnig as its new Chief Financial Officer (CFO).
He will succeed Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Robert Ottel, who has held the position on an interim basis since July 2025.
According to the company, Schuschnig will assume the CFO role on the Executive Board by 1 October 2026 at the latest.
His appointment will run for a three-year term.
Supervisory Board welcomes new appointment
Christian Reisinger, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Rosenbauer International AG, said: “We are very pleased to welcome Dr. Jörg Schuschnig, a seasoned financial expert with many years of industrial experience, to Rosenbauer International AG.
“It also allows us to coordinate better with neighbouring services.
“With his appointment, our executive board is now complete and excellently positioned to tackle the challenges of the coming years.
“Our shared goal remains to successfully continue developing Rosenbauer as the global market leader in firefighting sector.”
Schuschnig outlines priorities for financial strategy
Jörg Schuschnig, designated CFO of Rosenbauer International AG, said: “I am delighted to be taking on this new role at Rosenbauer – a company that, to me, stands for cutting-edge innovation, top-tier quality, and absolute reliability.
“Together with the team, I’m committed to further strengthening Rosenbauer’s financial stability and growth potential.
“A particular focus for me will be embedding efficiency and digital processes into our financial operations and advancing global governance to enhance our international competitiveness.”
Professional background and experience
Rosenbauer stated that Schuschnig brings extensive experience from a range of industrial and leadership roles.
Since 2022, he has served as Chief Financial Officer of the Coveris Group.
His previous positions include Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer of BGO Holding, as well as Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operating Officer at Bene.
Before that, he spent more than nine years at the Mondi Group, where he was a board member for its Industrial Bags and Consumer Flexibles business units.
Earlier in his career, he held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group.
Schuschnig holds a degree and a doctorate in Business Administration from WU Vienna.
Relevance for fire and safety professionals
Rosenbauer International AG is a key global supplier of firefighting vehicles, equipment and systems used by fire and rescue services worldwide.
The appointment of a new Chief Financial Officer indicates continuity and potential strategic development within the company’s financial and operational structure.
For procurement officers, fire chiefs and emergency service planners, the leadership transition may influence future investment strategies, production capabilities and global supply coordination across Rosenbauer’s product lines.
As the company continues to focus on efficiency and digitalisation, changes in its financial management could affect delivery schedules, pricing models and resource planning for large-scale fleet and equipment contracts.
This article was informed by information from the following source: Rosenbauer International AG

 He is a recognized financial expert with many years of international experience
 Focus on financial stability and sustainable growth of the Group
As announced by Rosenbauer International AG’s Supervisory Board in October 2025, Jörg Schuschnig has been appointed as the new Chief Financial Officer (CFO). He takes up his new role on April 1, 2026. Schuschnig succeeds CEO Robert Ottel, who had taken on the CFO agendas on an interim basis in addition to his work as Chief Executive Officer. The appointment is for a term of office of three years. 
“With Jörg Schuschnig, we are delighted to have acquired someone with profound financial expertise and many years of industry experience. The Executive Board team is now complete and in an excellent position to tackle the challenges of the years ahead. Our shared goal remains the successful further development of Rosenbauer as a global market leader in the firefighting industry,” said Christian Reisinger, Chairman of the Supervisory Board.
“I would like to thank the Supervisory Board for their confidence in me and look forward to working with my team and my colleagues on the Executive Board. Together, we will further strengthen Rosenbauer’s financial stability and harness the Group’s existing potential for further growth and increased earnings. I will focus in particular on consistently establishing efficient digital processes in the finance division, increasing efficiency, and further developing global governance within the company,” said CFO Jörg Schuschnig.
Schuschnig is a recognized financial expert with a doctorate in business administration and many years of international experience in various companies. He has been CFO of the Coveris Group since 2022. Previously, he was CEO and CFO of BGO Holding GmbH and CFO and COO of Bene GmbH. Before that, he spent around nine years with the Mondi Group, where he was an Executive Board member of the Industrial Bags and Consumer Flexibles business units. Earlier in his career, he held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group.

Rosenbauer appoints Jörg Schuschnig as Chief Financial Officer
Schuschnig to take up role by October 2026
Rosenbauer International AG has announced the appointment of Jörg Schuschnig as its new Chief Financial Officer (CFO).
He will succeed Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Robert Ottel, who has held the position on an interim basis since July 2025.
According to the company, Schuschnig will assume the CFO role on the Executive Board by 1 October 2026 at the latest.
His appointment will run for a three-year term.
Supervisory Board welcomes new appointment
Christian Reisinger, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Rosenbauer International AG, said: “We are very pleased to welcome Dr. Jörg Schuschnig, a seasoned financial expert with many years of industrial experience, to Rosenbauer International AG.
“It also allows us to coordinate better with neighbouring services.
“With his appointment, our executive board is now complete and excellently positioned to tackle the challenges of the coming years.
“Our shared goal remains to successfully continue developing Rosenbauer as the global market leader in firefighting sector.”
Schuschnig outlines priorities for financial strategy
Jörg Schuschnig, designated CFO of Rosenbauer International AG, said: “I am delighted to be taking on this new role at Rosenbauer – a company that, to me, stands for cutting-edge innovation, top-tier quality, and absolute reliability.
“Together with the team, I’m committed to further strengthening Rosenbauer’s financial stability and growth potential.
“A particular focus for me will be embedding efficiency and digital processes into our financial operations and advancing global governance to enhance our international competitiveness.”
Professional background and experience
Rosenbauer stated that Schuschnig brings extensive experience from a range of industrial and leadership roles.
Since 2022, he has served as Chief Financial Officer of the Coveris Group.
His previous positions include Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer of BGO Holding, as well as Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operating Officer at Bene.
Before that, he spent more than nine years at the Mondi Group, where he was a board member for its Industrial Bags and Consumer Flexibles business units.
Earlier in his career, he held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group.
Schuschnig holds a degree and a doctorate in Business Administration from WU Vienna.
Relevance for fire and safety professionals
Rosenbauer International AG is a key global supplier of firefighting vehicles, equipment and systems used by fire and rescue services worldwide.
The appointment of a new Chief Financial Officer indicates continuity and potential strategic development within the company’s financial and operational structure.
For procurement officers, fire chiefs and emergency service planners, the leadership transition may influence future investment strategies, production capabilities and global supply coordination across Rosenbauer’s product lines.
As the company continues to focus on efficiency and digitalisation, changes in its financial management could affect delivery schedules, pricing models and resource planning for large-scale fleet and equipment contracts.
This article was informed by information from the following source: Rosenbauer International AG

Rosenbauer reports record revenue EBIT and order backlog in 2025
Picture of Iain Hoey
Iain Hoey
Share this content
Facebook
Twitter
LinkedIn
Rosenbauer posts record 2025 results
Rosenbauer International AG reported record revenue, EBIT and order backlog for 2025, with sales rising to €1,429.0 million and order backlog reaching €2,354.6 million.
In a company statement published on 10 April 2026, Rosenbauer said EBIT rose to €84.5 million from €64.9 million in 2024, while earnings before taxes more than doubled to €54.7 million from €26.3 million.
Net profit for the period rose to €54.3 million from €29.8 million.
Cash flow from operating activities increased to €87.1 million from €82.2 million.
The equity ratio rose to 27.8% from 16.6%.
Net debt fell to €244.5 million from €392.5 million.
The net debt to EBITDA ratio fell to less than 2.
The company said vehicle deliveries to customers worldwide increased by around 4%.
Its Vehicles segment generated €1,115.8 million in revenue and accounted for around 78% of total revenue.
Trade working capital remained stable despite the increase in revenue.
Rosenbauer created 110 new jobs in Austria during 2025, bringing its global workforce to 4,922 employees as of 31 December.
Robert Ottel, Chief Executive Officer of Rosenbauer International AG, said: “2025 was a milestone for Rosenbauer.
“We achieved the strongest year in our company’s history, both operationally and financially, and at the same time laid the foundation for sustainable, profitable growth.
“Record sales, the doubling of our pre-tax earnings and the halving of our debt demonstrate our renewed strength.
“Strategically, we are focused on continuity: The Rosenbauer family remains committed to the company, and the new, future-minded anchor investors are strengthening Rosenbauer’s financial base.
“On this basis, we are further developing our business model in line with the three pillars of innovation and technology leadership, operational excellence, and consistent proximity to customers.
“I’m particularly proud of the 110 new jobs we’ve created in Austria.
“They symbolize the trust of our customers, the performance of our team, and our ambition to continue playing a decisive role in shaping the global firefighting industry as a global market leader,”
Financing and regional performance
Rosenbauer said the rise in earnings was linked to efficiency improvement measures, while financing costs fell after the capital increase and subsequent refinancing.
The financial result was €–29.9 million in 2025 compared with €–38.6 million in 2024.
Equity rose to €371.0 million at the end of 2025 from €208.1 million a year earlier.
Rosenbauer said it generates about one third of its revenue in the United States, where it produces for the local market at four of its own locations.
The company said it was affected only indirectly by trade policy restrictions in that region.
It added that temporary market uncertainties had a dampening effect on demand in the Americas region.
Order intake in the Americas region was €466.9 million, down from €529.6 million in the previous year.
Jörg Schuschnig, Chief Financial Officer of Rosenbauer International AG since April 1, 2026, said: “I am impressed by Rosenbauer’s performance over the past year.
“It shows how consistently the company is pursuing its course towards stability and profitability.
“My task is to further expand this financial strength, safeguard the quality of the balance sheet in the long term, and actively drive forward the transformation of our financial division.
“Rosenbauer has huge potential and I look forward to taking the next step in the financial and strategic development of the company together with the team,”
Rosenbauer sets out 2026 outlook
Rosenbauer said it started 2026 with an order backlog equal to around 165% of annual revenue and stated that 92.6% of revenue is generated outside Austria, with 53.5% generated outside Europe.
The company identified the US, India and South America as markets with long-term growth potential.
It said it is continuing to expand its customer service business and global service network.
Expansion at the Luckenwalde and Bad Abbach locations is intended to strengthen customer proximity and support the full vehicle life cycle.
Rosenbauer also said INTERSCHUTZ in Hanover will be a platform for presenting new solutions in e-mobility, forest fire deployment, equipment, vehicle concepts and fire extinguishing technology.
Based on current planning, the Executive Board expects sales of approximately €1.6 billion in 2026 and said the EBIT margin is expected to improve to more than 6%.
Rosenbauer expands global training capacity
Rosenbauer said on 18 March 2026 that it is expanding training capacity across its global network in response to increased demand for vehicle, equipment and service training.
The company said it operates training centres in Leonding, Karlsruhe, Dubai, Singapore and Wyoming.
More than 60 courses are offered in Leonding for service technicians, alongside expert sessions, customer training and internal staff development.
Training is focused on maintenance and servicing of Rosenbauer vehicles and products, as well as electronics, bodywork and assembly for employees and apprentices.
Rosenbauer also said it delivers on-site training at fire departments and provides e-learning programmes for operators.
It added that infrastructure at the Leonding site has been expanded with two indoor vehicle training bays, an additional workshop and new training rooms.
Rosenbauer appoints Jörg Schuschnig as CFO
Rosenbauer International AG said on 1 April 2026 that Jörg Schuschnig has taken up the role of Chief Financial Officer for a three-year term.
He succeeds Chief Executive Officer Robert Ottel, who had been handling the CFO remit on an interim basis.
The company said Schuschnig has international financial experience and previously served as CFO of the Coveris Group since 2022.
He has also held roles as CEO and CFO of BGO Holding GmbH and CFO and COO of Bene GmbH.
Earlier in his career, he spent around nine years with the Mondi Group and held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group.
Rosenbauer appoints Barbara Gassner as HR lead
Rosenbauer International AG also said on 1 April 2026 that Barbara Gassner has been appointed Senior Vice President Human Resources.
She is responsible for the Group’s global HR agendas.
The company said Gassner brings international HR experience across industrial organisations.
Her focus includes corporate culture, talent and executive development, and performance management.
Gassner previously served as Head of Group HR at the Max Aicher Group in Bavaria.
She has also held roles at AustroCel Hallein GmbH and INTERSPAR GmbH.

Portrait Jörg Schuschnig
 He is a recognized financial expert with many years of international experience
 Focus on financial stability and sustainable growth of the Group
As announced by Rosenbauer International AG’s Supervisory Board in October 2025, Jörg Schuschnig has been appointed as the new Chief Financial Officer (CFO). He takes up his new role on April 1, 2026. Schuschnig succeeds CEO Robert Ottel, who had taken on the CFO agendas on an interim basis in addition to his work as Chief Executive Officer. The appointment is for a term of office of three years. 
“With Jörg Schuschnig, we are delighted to have acquired someone with profound financial expertise and many years of industry experience. The Executive Board team is now complete and in an excellent position to tackle the challenges of the years ahead. Our shared goal remains the successful further development of Rosenbauer as a global market leader in the firefighting industry,” said Christian Reisinger, Chairman of the Supervisory Board.
“I would like to thank the Supervisory Board for their confidence in me and look forward to working with my team and my colleagues on the Executive Board. Together, we will further strengthen Rosenbauer’s financial stability and harness the Group’s existing potential for further growth and increased earnings. I will focus in particular on consistently establishing efficient digital processes in the finance division, increasing efficiency, and further developing global governance within the company,” said CFO Jörg Schuschnig.
Schuschnig is a recognized financial expert with a doctorate in business administration and many years of international experience in various companies. He has been CFO of the Coveris Group since 2022. Previously, he was CEO and CFO of BGO Holding GmbH and CFO and COO of Bene GmbH. Before that, he spent around nine years with the Mondi Group, where he was an Executive Board member of the Industrial Bags and Consumer Flexibles business units. Earlier in his career, he held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group.

Jörg Schuschnig (55) ist neuer CFO bei Rosenbauer
Veröffentlicht von  Dr. Marco Henry V. Neumueller
Wie der Aufsichtsrat der Rosenbauer International AG bereits im Oktober 2025 bekanntgegeben hatte, wurde Jörg Schuschnig zum neuen Finanzvorstand (CFO) bestellt. Er hat seine Funktion mit 1. April 2026 angetreten. Schuschnig folgt auf CEO Robert Ottel, der die CFO-Agenden zusätzlich zu seiner Tätigkeit als Vorstandsvorsitzender interimistisch wahrgenommen hatte. Die Bestellung erfolgt für eine Funktionsperiode von drei Jahren.
„Wir freuen uns sehr, mit Jörg Schuschnig einen profunden Finanzexperten mit langjähriger Industrieerfahrung gewonnen zu haben. Das Vorstandsteam ist damit komplettiert und exzellent aufgestellt, um die Herausforderungen der nächsten Jahre zu meistern. Unser gemeinsames Ziel bleibt es, Rosenbauer als globalen Marktführer im Feuerwehrbereich erfolgreich weiterzuentwickeln“, sagt Aufsichtsratsvorsitzender Christian Reisinger.
„Ich danke dem Aufsichtsrat für sein Vertrauen und freue mich sehr auf die Zusammenarbeit mit meinen Vorstandskollegen und meinem Team. Gemeinsam werden wir die finanzielle Stabilität von Rosenbauer weiter stärken und das vorhandene Potential der Gruppe für weiteres Wachstum und Ertragssteigerung nutzen. Mein besonderer Fokus liegt darauf, leistungsfähige digitale Prozesse im Finanzbereich durchgängig zu etablieren, die Effizienz zu steigern und die globale Governance im Unternehmen weiterzuentwickeln“, so CFO Jörg Schuschnig.
Als ausgewiesener Finanzexperte verfügt der promovierte Betriebswirt über langjährige internationale Erfahrung in unterschiedlichen Unternehmen. Seit 2022 war er als CFO der Coveris Group tätig. Zuvor war er CEO und CFO der BGO Holding GmbH sowie CFO und COO der Bene GmbH. Davor verbrachte er rund neun Jahre in der Mondi Group, unter anderem im Vorstand der Business Units Industrial Bags und Consumer Flexibles. Frühere berufliche Stationen hatten ihn zur Mayr-Melnhof Gruppe geführt.
Über das Familienunternehmen Rosenbauer Gruppe
Rosenbauer ist ein international tätiger Konzern und verlässlicher Partner der Feuerwehren auf der ganzen Welt. Das Unternehmen entwickelt und produziert Fahrzeuge, Löschtechnik, Ausrüstung und digitale Lösungen für Berufs-, Betriebs-, Werk- und freiwillige Feuerwehren sowie Anlagen für den vorbeugenden Brandschutz. In ungefähr 110 Ländern ist Rosenbauer mit einem Vertriebs- und Servicenetzwerk vertreten. Mit einem Umsatz von 1,3 Mrd. € und rund 4.500 Mitarbeitenden (Stand: 31. Dezember 2024) ist der Konzern der größte Feuerwehrausstatter der Welt.

As announced by Rosenbauer International AG’s Supervisory Board in October 2025, Jörg Schuschnig has been appointed as the new Chief Financial Officer (CFO).
Portrait Jörg Schuschnig
 He is a recognized financial expert with many years of international experience
 Focus on financial stability and sustainable growth of the Group
As announced by Rosenbauer International AG’s Supervisory Board in October 2025, Jörg Schuschnig has been appointed as the new Chief Financial Officer (CFO). He takes up his new role on April 1, 2026. Schuschnig succeeds CEO Robert Ottel, who had taken on the CFO agendas on an interim basis in addition to his work as Chief Executive Officer. The appointment is for a term of office of three years. 
“With Jörg Schuschnig, we are delighted to have acquired someone with profound financial expertise and many years of industry experience. The Executive Board team is now complete and in an excellent position to tackle the challenges of the years ahead. Our shared goal remains the successful further development of Rosenbauer as a global market leader in the firefighting industry,” said Christian Reisinger, Chairman of the Supervisory Board.
“I would like to thank the Supervisory Board for their confidence in me and look forward to working with my team and my colleagues on the Executive Board. Together, we will further strengthen Rosenbauer’s financial stability and harness the Group’s existing potential for further growth and increased earnings. I will focus in particular on consistently establishing efficient digital processes in the finance division, increasing efficiency, and further developing global governance within the company,” said CFO Jörg Schuschnig.
Schuschnig is a recognized financial expert with a doctorate in business administration and many years of international experience in various companies. He has been CFO of the Coveris Group since 2022. Previously, he was CEO and CFO of BGO Holding GmbH and CFO and COO of Bene GmbH. Before that, he spent around nine years with the Mondi Group, where he was an Executive Board member of the Industrial Bags and Consumer Flexibles business units. Earlier in his career, he held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group.

Jörg Schuschnig (55) ist neuer CFO bei Rosenbauer
Veröffentlicht von  Dr. Marco Henry V. Neumueller
Wie der Aufsichtsrat der Rosenbauer International AG bereits im Oktober 2025 bekanntgegeben hatte, wurde Jörg Schuschnig zum neuen Finanzvorstand (CFO) bestellt. Er hat seine Funktion mit 1. April 2026 angetreten. Schuschnig folgt auf CEO Robert Ottel, der die CFO-Agenden zusätzlich zu seiner Tätigkeit als Vorstandsvorsitzender interimistisch wahrgenommen hatte. Die Bestellung erfolgt für eine Funktionsperiode von drei Jahren.
„Wir freuen uns sehr, mit Jörg Schuschnig einen profunden Finanzexperten mit langjähriger Industrieerfahrung gewonnen zu haben. Das Vorstandsteam ist damit komplettiert und exzellent aufgestellt, um die Herausforderungen der nächsten Jahre zu meistern. Unser gemeinsames Ziel bleibt es, Rosenbauer als globalen Marktführer im Feuerwehrbereich erfolgreich weiterzuentwickeln“, sagt Aufsichtsratsvorsitzender Christian Reisinger.
„Ich danke dem Aufsichtsrat für sein Vertrauen und freue mich sehr auf die Zusammenarbeit mit meinen Vorstandskollegen und meinem Team. Gemeinsam werden wir die finanzielle Stabilität von Rosenbauer weiter stärken und das vorhandene Potential der Gruppe für weiteres Wachstum und Ertragssteigerung nutzen. Mein besonderer Fokus liegt darauf, leistungsfähige digitale Prozesse im Finanzbereich durchgängig zu etablieren, die Effizienz zu steigern und die globale Governance im Unternehmen weiterzuentwickeln“, so CFO Jörg Schuschnig.
Als ausgewiesener Finanzexperte verfügt der promovierte Betriebswirt über langjährige internationale Erfahrung in unterschiedlichen Unternehmen. Seit 2022 war er als CFO der Coveris Group tätig. Zuvor war er CEO und CFO der BGO Holding GmbH sowie CFO und COO der Bene GmbH. Davor verbrachte er rund neun Jahre in der Mondi Group, unter anderem im Vorstand der Business Units Industrial Bags und Consumer Flexibles. Frühere berufliche Stationen hatten ihn zur Mayr-Melnhof Gruppe geführt.
Über das Familienunternehmen Rosenbauer Gruppe
Rosenbauer ist ein international tätiger Konzern und verlässlicher Partner der Feuerwehren auf der ganzen Welt. Das Unternehmen entwickelt und produziert Fahrzeuge, Löschtechnik, Ausrüstung und digitale Lösungen für Berufs-, Betriebs-, Werk- und freiwillige Feuerwehren sowie Anlagen für den vorbeugenden Brandschutz. In ungefähr 110 Ländern ist Rosenbauer mit einem Vertriebs- und Servicenetzwerk vertreten. Mit einem Umsatz von 1,3 Mrd. € und rund 4.500 Mitarbeitenden (Stand: 31. Dezember 2024) ist der Konzern der größte Feuerwehrausstatter der Welt.

Rosenbauer reports record revenue EBIT and order backlog in 2025
Picture of Iain Hoey
Iain Hoey
Share this content
Facebook
Twitter
LinkedIn
Rosenbauer posts record 2025 results
Rosenbauer International AG reported record revenue, EBIT and order backlog for 2025, with sales rising to €1,429.0 million and order backlog reaching €2,354.6 million.
In a company statement published on 10 April 2026, Rosenbauer said EBIT rose to €84.5 million from €64.9 million in 2024, while earnings before taxes more than doubled to €54.7 million from €26.3 million.
Net profit for the period rose to €54.3 million from €29.8 million.
Cash flow from operating activities increased to €87.1 million from €82.2 million.
The equity ratio rose to 27.8% from 16.6%.
Net debt fell to €244.5 million from €392.5 million.
The net debt to EBITDA ratio fell to less than 2.
The company said vehicle deliveries to customers worldwide increased by around 4%.
Its Vehicles segment generated €1,115.8 million in revenue and accounted for around 78% of total revenue.
Trade working capital remained stable despite the increase in revenue.
Rosenbauer created 110 new jobs in Austria during 2025, bringing its global workforce to 4,922 employees as of 31 December.
Robert Ottel, Chief Executive Officer of Rosenbauer International AG, said: “2025 was a milestone for Rosenbauer.
“We achieved the strongest year in our company’s history, both operationally and financially, and at the same time laid the foundation for sustainable, profitable growth.
“Record sales, the doubling of our pre-tax earnings and the halving of our debt demonstrate our renewed strength.
“Strategically, we are focused on continuity: The Rosenbauer family remains committed to the company, and the new, future-minded anchor investors are strengthening Rosenbauer’s financial base.
“On this basis, we are further developing our business model in line with the three pillars of innovation and technology leadership, operational excellence, and consistent proximity to customers.
“I’m particularly proud of the 110 new jobs we’ve created in Austria.
“They symbolize the trust of our customers, the performance of our team, and our ambition to continue playing a decisive role in shaping the global firefighting industry as a global market leader,”
Financing and regional performance
Rosenbauer said the rise in earnings was linked to efficiency improvement measures, while financing costs fell after the capital increase and subsequent refinancing.
The financial result was €–29.9 million in 2025 compared with €–38.6 million in 2024.
Equity rose to €371.0 million at the end of 2025 from €208.1 million a year earlier.
Rosenbauer said it generates about one third of its revenue in the United States, where it produces for the local market at four of its own locations.
The company said it was affected only indirectly by trade policy restrictions in that region.
It added that temporary market uncertainties had a dampening effect on demand in the Americas region.
Order intake in the Americas region was €466.9 million, down from €529.6 million in the previous year.
Jörg Schuschnig, Chief Financial Officer of Rosenbauer International AG since April 1, 2026, said: “I am impressed by Rosenbauer’s performance over the past year.
“It shows how consistently the company is pursuing its course towards stability and profitability.
“My task is to further expand this financial strength, safeguard the quality of the balance sheet in the long term, and actively drive forward the transformation of our financial division.
“Rosenbauer has huge potential and I look forward to taking the next step in the financial and strategic development of the company together with the team,”
Rosenbauer sets out 2026 outlook
Rosenbauer said it started 2026 with an order backlog equal to around 165% of annual revenue and stated that 92.6% of revenue is generated outside Austria, with 53.5% generated outside Europe.
The company identified the US, India and South America as markets with long-term growth potential.
It said it is continuing to expand its customer service business and global service network.
Expansion at the Luckenwalde and Bad Abbach locations is intended to strengthen customer proximity and support the full vehicle life cycle.
Rosenbauer also said INTERSCHUTZ in Hanover will be a platform for presenting new solutions in e-mobility, forest fire deployment, equipment, vehicle concepts and fire extinguishing technology.
Based on current planning, the Executive Board expects sales of approximately €1.6 billion in 2026 and said the EBIT margin is expected to improve to more than 6%.
Rosenbauer expands global training capacity
Rosenbauer said on 18 March 2026 that it is expanding training capacity across its global network in response to increased demand for vehicle, equipment and service training.
The company said it operates training centres in Leonding, Karlsruhe, Dubai, Singapore and Wyoming.
More than 60 courses are offered in Leonding for service technicians, alongside expert sessions, customer training and internal staff development.
Training is focused on maintenance and servicing of Rosenbauer vehicles and products, as well as electronics, bodywork and assembly for employees and apprentices.
Rosenbauer also said it delivers on-site training at fire departments and provides e-learning programmes for operators.
It added that infrastructure at the Leonding site has been expanded with two indoor vehicle training bays, an additional workshop and new training rooms.
Rosenbauer appoints Jörg Schuschnig as CFO
Rosenbauer International AG said on 1 April 2026 that Jörg Schuschnig has taken up the role of Chief Financial Officer for a three-year term.
He succeeds Chief Executive Officer Robert Ottel, who had been handling the CFO remit on an interim basis.
The company said Schuschnig has international financial experience and previously served as CFO of the Coveris Group since 2022.
He has also held roles as CEO and CFO of BGO Holding GmbH and CFO and COO of Bene GmbH.
Earlier in his career, he spent around nine years with the Mondi Group and held positions at the Mayr-Melnhof Group.
Rosenbauer appoints Barbara Gassner as HR lead
Rosenbauer International AG also said on 1 April 2026 that Barbara Gassner has been appointed Senior Vice President Human Resources.
She is responsible for the Group’s global HR agendas.
The company said Gassner brings international HR experience across industrial organisations.
Her focus includes corporate culture, talent and executive development, and performance management.
Gassner previously served as Head of Group HR at the Max Aicher Group in Bavaria.
She has also held roles at AustroCel Hallein GmbH and INTERSPAR GmbH.

Press image
 Revenues rise by 3.5% despite operational and geopolitical pressures
 EBIT almost triples to €20.4 million
 Order intake of €717.8 million confirms strong demand
 Long-term financing secured early and financing facility expanded to €339 million

The Rosenbauer Group generated revenues of €625.9 million in the first half of 2026 (1–6/2025: €604.7 million) and successfully continued its growth trajectory with an increase of 3.5% year-on-year. The drivers of growth are a higher number of vehicle deliveries and more business in Preventive Fire Protection. In the first half of 2026, consolidated revenues were 48.3% in the Europe area, 31.9% in the Americas area, 9.0% in the Asia-Pacific area, and 8.8% in the Middle East & Africa area. Preventive Fire Protection contributed 2.0% to revenues.
Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and the associated uncertainties in transportation and delivery routes, especially in connection with the Strait of Hormuz, led to delays in deliveries in certain projects. In addition, SAP S/4HANA was introduced in the main Austrian companies in April 2026. The introduction was an important step toward modernizing the process landscape. However, the transition led to operational delays to individual deliveries. Both factors negatively impacted assets, liabilities, financial position, and profit or loss in the reporting period.
Financial performance
The increased business volume and improved contribution margins for vehicles resulted in a significantly stronger operating result. EBITDA increased to €38.8 million (1–6/2025: €28.2 million), while EBIT nearly tripled to €20.4million (1–6/2025: €7.4 million). EBT improved to €11.1 million (1–6/2025: €-10.5 million).
Orders
Order intake was €717.8 million in the first half of 2026 (1–6/2025: €705.2 million) and thus remained at a high level. In particular, the areas Europe and Middle East & Africa increased its order intake. In the US, discussions about tariffs and retaliatory tariffs adversely affected dealers’ ordering behavior.
The order backlog increased to €2,434.4 million as of June 30, 2026 (June 30, 2025: €2,351.5 million). With this order book, the Rosenbauer Group has a solid starting point from which to drive forward further profitable revenue growth.
As of June 30, 2026, Rosenbauer had a global workforce of 5,039 employees, 371 more than in the previous year (June 30, 2025: 4,668).
Financial and net assets position
In the first half of 2026, the financial and net assets position was particularly impacted by delayed deliveries due to geopolitical uncertainties and the introduction of SAP S/4HANA. At €328.5 million, net debt as of June 30, 2026, was at a similar level to the previous year (June 30, 2025: €314.3 million). The delivery delays led to an increase in trade working capital to €586.2 million (1–6/2025: €477.4 million) and impacted operating cash flow, which amounted to €-60.5 million (1–6/2025: €-23.8 million). Rosenbauer continues to expect positive operating cash flow for 2026 as a whole.
In early August, 2026, a financing agreement was concluded with the current banking consortium of Rosenbauer International AG for the early extension and increase of the existing syndicated loan. A financing volume of €339million (December 31, 2025: €330 million) was agreed with a term until August 2029 (December 31, 2025: March 2028) and the option to extend for a further two years (1+1).
“The first half of 2026 shows that Rosenbauer is growing successfully even under challenging conditions. Despite geopolitical uncertainties in the Middle East and additional expenses resulting from the launch of SAP S/4HANA, we were able to boost revenues by 3.5%.
The SAP transformation at the Austrian sites that started in April 2026 is an important step toward modernizing our processes and improving our customer service. However, the transition led to challenges in production planning and delays in deliveries. We regret the resulting delivery delays and are aware of our responsibility for our customers’ operational readiness. That’s why we have increased our staffing capacity in specific areas and are working at full speed to gradually reduce the backlog and get our customers up and running again quickly.
The SAP launch remains challenging but deliveries are steadily improving. We expect operations to largely return to normal in the coming months. Continued strong demand for our products underscores the robustness of our business and boosts our confidence for the second half of the year,” says Robert Ottel, CEO of Rosenbauer International AG.
“The significant increase in our EBIT to €20.4 million and the improvement in the gross profit margin to 20.6% demonstrate the success of our attentive customer service, our strong market presence, and the ongoing improvement of our processes. With an equity ratio of 26.3% and an order intake of €717.8 million, we have a solid financial base and a very good starting point for further business development. The high order backlog ensures planning certainty in the coming quarters. Despite temporarily strained operating cash flow, we consider Rosenbauer to be in a very good financial and operational position,” says Jörg Schuschnig, CFO of Rosenbauer International AG.
Outlook
Demand for Rosenbauer’s products remains robust worldwide. With an order intake of €717.8 million in the first half of the year and an order backlog of €2.4 billion, the Group has a solid foundation for the second half of the year. At the same time, there are risks from geopolitical tensions, a volatile market environment, and possible disruptions to supply chains. These factors may impact material availability, cost development, and business performance.
Despite these uncertainties, the Group’s Executive Board anticipates further revenue and earnings growth in the 2026 financial year. Revenue is expected to reach up to €1.6 billion, with the EBIT margin increasing to over 6%.

Record year with all-time highs in revenue, EBITDA, and EBIT plus a record order backlog
Press picture 1

 Debt halved, Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio reduced to below 2
 Revenue grows to €1,429 million and reaches all-time high
 Trade working capital stable despite higher revenue
 Record order backlog of €2,354.6 million and 110 new jobs created in Austria

Overall development for 2025 was very positive for Rosenbauer. Firstly, the order backlog rose to €2,354.6 million (2024: €2,279.8 million), well above the Group’s annual revenues. Secondly, sales rose by 9.4% to €1,429.0 million and earnings rose to €84.5 million. With the successful capital increase and the completed refinancing deal, Rosenbauer has also strengthened its financial base and created important conditions for the company’s future development.
RevenuesAt €1,429.0 million, revenues in 2025 were 9.4% higher than the previous year’s level (2024: €1,305.9 million). Vehicle deliveries to customers worldwide increased by approximately 4%. The Group’s strongest product segment in terms of revenues was Vehicles, with a share of revenue of around 78% (2024: 75%) and revenue of €1,115.8 million.
Result of operationsThe efficiency improvement measures contributed substantially to the increase in the EBIT to €84.5 million in the 2025 financial year (2024: €64.9 million).The financing costs dropped in the 2025 financial year due to the capital increase and the subsequent refinancing, resulting in a financial result of €–29.9 million (2024: €–38.6 million).
Earnings before taxes (EBT) amounted to €54.7 million (2024: €26.3 million). This resulted in a substantially positive result for the period of €54.3 million (2024: €29.8 million).
Rosenbauer generates about one third of its revenue in the United States, where it produces for the local market at four of its own locations. As a result, Rosenbauer in the region is affected only indirectly by trade policy restrictions. Temporary market uncertainties had a dampening effect on demand in the Americas region nonetheless. At €466.9 million, the order intake was lower than the previous year’s level of €529.6 million.
FinancingEquity as of December 31, 2025, was €371.0 million (2024: €208.1 million). The equity ratio rose to 27.8% (2024: 16.6%) due to the capital increase and profit after tax. At the same time, net debt in the reporting year dropped significantly to €244.5 million (2024: €392.5 million), which also improved the net debt to EBITDA ratio to a factor of less than 2.
“2025 was a milestone for Rosenbauer. We achieved the strongest year in our company’s history, both operationally and financially, and at the same time laid the foundation for sustainable, profitable growth. Record sales, the doubling of our pre-tax earnings and the halving of our debt demonstrate our renewed strength.
Strategically, we are focused on continuity: The Rosenbauer family remains committed to the company, and the new, future-minded anchor investors are strengthening Rosenbauer’s financial base. On this basis, we are further developing our business model in line with the three pillars of innovation and technology leadership, operational excellence, and consistent proximity to customers.
I’m particularly proud of the 110 new jobs we’ve created in Austria. They symbolize the trust of our customers, the performance of our team, and our ambition to continue playing a decisive role in shaping the global firefighting industry as a global market leader,” said Robert Ottel, CEO of Rosenbauer International AG.
“I am impressed by Rosenbauer’s performance over the past year. It shows how consistently the company is pursuing its course towards stability and profitability. My task is to further expand this financial strength, safeguard the quality of the balance sheet in the long term, and actively drive forward the transformation of our financial division. Rosenbauer has huge potential and I look forward to taking the next step in the financial and strategic development of the company together with the team,” said Jörg Schuschnig, CFO of Rosenbauer International AG since April 1, 2026.
Stable development and growth in 2026Rosenbauer started 2026 in an excellent position. In Austria alone, 110 new jobs were created in 2025, bringing the global workforce to 4,922 employees. The historically high order backlog of €2,354.6 million – around 165% of annual revenue – provides a solid foundation for business development well beyond the current year.
Internationalization is being consistently pursued: 92.6% of revenue is generated outside Austria and 53.5% outside Europe. Rosenbauer sees strong potential for long-term growth particularly in the US, India, and South America.
In parallel, the company is continuing to invest in expanding its customer service business and its global service network. Expansion at the Luckenwalde and Bad Abbach locations strengthens the company’s proximity to customers and its focus on the entire vehicle life cycle.
Numerous product and technology innovations will also dominate 2026. The world’s leading trade fair for INTERSCHUTZ firefighting technology in Hanover will provide Rosenbauer with a central platform for presenting new solutions in the fields of e-mobility, forest fire deployment, and equipment as well as state-of-the-art vehicle concepts and fire extinguishing technology.
OutlookBased on current planning, the Executive Board expects sales of approximately  €1.6 billion for the 2026 financial year. Taking into account the existing uncertainties, the EBIT margin is expected to continue to improve to over 6%.

In the first quarter of 2026, the Rosenbauer Group continued its growth trajectory and generated revenues of €303.8 million (1–3/2025: €263.6 million), an increase of 15.3% compared with the same period of the previous year. This was due in particular to the higher number of vehicle deliveries and improved business volume in the areas of equipment, service, and Preventive Fire Protection. With growth of 16.8%, the Vehicles product segment recorded the strongest increase. 
The higher business volume and improved contribution margins for vehicles delivered led to a significant increase in the operating result. EBITDA rose to €23.0 million (1–3/2025: €16.7 million) and EBIT amounted to €14.4 million (1–3/2025: €9.0 million). At the end of the reporting period, the Group’s EBT reached a pleasing €10.4 million (1–3/2025: €1.8 million) and net profit was €9.4 million, considerably higher than the previous year’s figure (1–3/2025: €0.1 million).
“The significant improvement in EBIT, EBT, and net profit in the first quarter underscores the current high demand and the increasing number of vehicle deliveries in the firefighting business. At the same time, the continued high order backlog – which exceeds our annual turnover – demonstrates persistently strong market demand and gives us a good basis for planning future business development,” said Robert Ottel, CEO of Rosenbauer International AG.
Revenues and result of operations
Revenues in the first quarter of 2026 stood at €303.8 million (1–3/2025: €263.6 million). Consolidated revenues were spread across the different sales regions as follows: Europe area 50%, Americas area 31%, Asia-Pacific area 9%, Middle East & Africa area 8%, and the Preventive Fire Protection segment 2%.
From January to March 2026, the Rosenbauer Group recorded another pleasing order intake of €342.9 million (1–3/2025: €358.7 million), which exceeded the revenues of €303.8 million achieved in the same period. The Europe area and the Preventive Fire Protection (PFP) segment succeeded in boosting their order intake, while orders in the Americas area remained roughly at the same level as the previous year. Incoming orders in the Middle East & Africa and Asia-Pacific areas were lower than the previous year’s figure. 
The order backlog remained almost unchanged at €2,348.3 million at the end of the first quarter of 2026 (March 31, 2025: €2,343.5 million). With this order book, the Rosenbauer Group has a solid basis for further profitable revenue growth.
Financial and net assets position
Net debt increased to €301.1 million from the previous year’s figure of €288.0 million. The main driver of this was the increase in trade working capital to €557.1 million (1–3/2025: €464.7 million), which involved additional financing requirements. The equity ratio, however, improved to 27.0% (Q1–Q3 2025: 25.2%).
At €-41.4 million (1–3/2025: €-6.8 million), cash flow from operating activities remained negative in the first quarter due to the increase in production and the associated higher trade working capital. Cash flow is therefore negatively impacted in the short term due to growth. However, positive cash flow from operating activities is expected for 2026 as a whole.
Outlook
Sector development is stable at the start of 2026. Well-filled order books and stabilized supply chains are supporting both production and delivery and providing a solid basis for positive revenue development over the course of the year. At the same time there are uncertainties, particularly with regard to public investment budgets, trade policy and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.
The Group’s Executive Board thus expects sales and earnings to increase further in 2026 and anticipates revenues of around €1.6 billion. Taking existing uncertainties into account, the EBIT margin is expected to continue to improve to over 6%.

E-Mobility
The answer is electric. Find out why the future at Rosenbauer is electrified.
Learn more
The future is electric
Moving solutions thanks to alternative drive concepts
A rethink is taking place. In politics, cooperation, a wide variety of industries – indeed, in each and every individual. As market leaders, we see it as our responsibility not only to support this positive trend, but to expand it. That's why Rosenbauer is making a sustainable contribution to the fire service industry: with battery-powered electric drive concepts. We see the future in “e-mobility” as a synonym for alternative drive concepts.
With innovative technologies we are actively shaping change and setting new standards for firefighting operation. Our electric drive concepts enable both driving and firefighting operations without propulsion-related exhaust emissions, as long as the vehicle is powered exclusively by the battery.
the panther electric
A new era begins
Electrifying developments for the future
Our products
Our target as market leader is to develop the most effective and future-proof system solutions for the fire service industry. Through the consistent electrification of our fire engines and equipment, we are ready for tomorrow today. Even if energy supply continues to evolve, hybrid technologies will emerge that rely on an electric drive architecture.
Image: red RT on stage with blue lighting
A milestone in firefighting.
Image: Black PANTHER electric on stage with blue lighting
## PANTHER electric
A new era begins.
L32A-Xs electric against a blue background
## L32A-XS electric
The World Innovation
Our products in use
Customer Stories
Skip slider
RT on the new bridge in Linz
E-mobility thought through from A to Z
A groundbreaking idea, born long before politics, media and society not just suggested but demanded a change in thinking. Rosenbauer has always been a trailblazer, an innovator and an outside-the-box thinker in disaster protection.
Read more (Opens in new tab)
Side view of the Vancouver Fire Department's RTX
Endurance test in Canada
On paper, the RTX's features look impressive. In Vancouver, the city of contrasts, the emergency vehicle has to prove itself. Canada's eighth largest city presents him with countless challenges.
Read more (Opens in new tab)
Close-up: two fire engines of the BF Basel
Grüezi in Switzerland
Basel-city, the canton in northwestern Switzerland bordering France and Germany, has earned this title. The first fully electric police cars were purchased in 2019. And other authorities are also turning to electric drive.
Read more (Opens in new tab)
RT on the street in front of several houses
Why e-mobility in the firefighting industry?
We did not take the decision lightly. It was based on a number of factors that took both ecological and economic aspects into account. Here we would like to show why Rosenbauer considers e-mobility to be the right technology for the future of the firefighting industry.
Read more (Opens in new tab)
Front view of the RT on a road in a rural area at full speed.
Immediate impact in action
Firefighters worldwide literally walk through fire for us every day. They are there when we need them. And Rosenbauer is there for these people. Always striving to make operations even safer and more efficient.
Read more (Opens in new tab)
RT vehicle at sunset
Changing today for tomorrow
Low-noise and locally emission-free – these are the obvious benefits our innovative drive concept has. But the implications reach much further. Locally, globally, and also in people's minds, something is being ignited. Something of central importance for the future.
Read more (Opens in new tab)
Detailed view of the RT electric 
Investing in the future. Benefiting in the long term.
Let's take the future into our own hands. Guided by sustainable technology that shows us the right path. We continuously refine and develop it further, while boldly moving ahead. The PANTHER electric already demonstrates how innovative drive concepts can combine sustainable mobility with full operational capability: driving and pumping functions can be powered entirely by batteries, while a diesel backup system ensures maximum reliability whenever additional energy is required. Join us on this journey toward a future that is both sustainable and secure.
Read more (Opens in new tab)
Service employee working in front of a laptop
Intelligent Services. Unbound Readiness.
Rosenbauer not only responds to the challenges of today's world in the development of alternative drive concepts. The customer service is being adjusted accordingly.
Read more (Opens in new tab)
Front view of the RT in the open air
Efficiency, measured by the degree of efficiency
A groundbreaking idea, born long before politics, media and society not just suggested but demanded a change in thinking. Rosenbauer has always been a trailblazer, an innovator and an outside-the-box thinker in disaster protection.
Read more (Opens in new tab)
Rosenbauer lettering on the office building at sunset
Living sustainability in society
E-mobility promotes sustainability through lower emissions and greater resource conservation. Rosenbauer uses this technology to develop more environmentally friendly and efficient emergency vehicles. For example, in the PANTHER electric, driving and pumping functions can be operated using battery-electric power. A diesel backup system is available to provide additional energy when needed.
Read more (Opens in new tab)
Side view of the yellow PANTHER electric at Dallas Airport
Dallas Love Field Airport
Dallas Love Field is making history: In 2025, the airport will be the first in the world to put the all-electric PANTHER 6x6 electric into operation. This is made possible by a groundbreaking partnership between Rosenbauer America and the Dallas fire service, who are jointly developing the innovative aircraft rescue & fire fighting vehicle until it is ready for series production.
Read more (Opens in new tab)
Jump to slider start

The future is electric
Energy- & Charging Infrastructure
Climate change is a reality, and a manmade one at that. Global temperatures are rising, and extreme weather events are increasing. The consequences are noticeable: floods, heat waves, and power outages, which also endanger critical infrastructure such as fire stations.
This means that infrastructure must not only be climate-friendly, but also resilient. Climate adaptation is just as important as climate protection. A resilient energy and mobility infrastructure protects against failures and ensures operational readiness, even in times of crisis. These necessary steps can be achieved through the energy and mobility transition.
Learn more
the answer is electric
Our path to electromobility
Skip slider
The RT: An idea becomes reality
The journey begins
In 2011, the first considerations about alternative drive concepts were voiced. We address future challenges and develop scenarios in a wide range of areas. The foundations for the RT and the trend map are laid.
Graphic of the Fire Department Trendmap 5.0
The RT: An idea becomes reality
The Concept Fire Truck
In 2016, the CFT will be presented as chassis of the 150th anniversary celebrations. The idea of e-mobility in firefighting thus becomes tangible and can be experienced.
Concept Fire Truck in front of modern building
The RT: An idea becomes reality
The launch event
In 2020 the time has come: The RT will be officially presented in Linz. The event is a complete success. Positive feedback and awards for the RT confirm the path we have chosen.
RT on stage at the launch event
The RT: An idea becomes reality
Convincing test phase
The RT is undergoing a 13-month test phase with the Berlin Fire Department. The result: round bar 1,400 deployments, on busy days up to 16 times within 24 hours, without fault and usually without intermediate charging. Over 90% of all operations could be completed purely electrically. The RT is taken over into regular operation.
Close-up of the Rosenbauer logo on the RT
The RT: An idea becomes reality
RTX goes America
The first RTX (RT in US design) will be delivered in 2022. In a short test phase, over 98% of all operations could be carried out electrically. And since September 2022, the RTX has been portion of the regular vehicle fleet in Los Angeles City.
Three RTX side by side on the FDIC
10 Years of Technology Development - World Premiere at Interschutz
The Rosenbauer Electric Line-Up
The Rosenbauer E-Lineup will celebrate its premiere at Interschutz 2022. The fully electric PANTHER electric combines maximum performance with sustainable technology and enables multiple uses on a single charge. The RT revolutionizes municipal firefighting operation with its compact, maneuverable construction and a fully integrated cabin for optimal ergonomics and safety.
Rosenbauer electric lineup at Interschutz
Proven functionalities. Future-oriented technology.
The PANTHER electric
Available to order since 2024: The PANTHER electric combines proven wattage with future-oriented technology. Thanks to the fully electric drive and Energy Backup System, multiple uses per charge are possible – without compromising on speed, wattage and safety.
PANTHER electric on runway
Jump to slider start
Advantages of new technologies
E-mobility in firefighting technology
Three firefighters discuss in the cockpit of the RT
Noise reduction
Electric vehicles are very quiet. This leads to less noise pollution in cities and residential areas, which improves the quality of life of residents. Less noise also means that emergency services can react more attentively and quickly in emergency situations.
Red RT driving on a bridge
No local emissions
In purely battery-electric operation, no propulsion-related exhaust emissions are generated. If the diesel-powered backup system is used, exhaust emissions are produced. This is particularly beneficial in urban areas where air quality is often a major problem.
Close-up of a side Rosenbauer logo on an RT
Alternative uses
Another advantage of e-mobility is the possibility of bidirectional use, such as Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G). This technology enables electric vehicles not only to draw energy from the grid but also to feed excess energy back into the grid. This contributes to the stabilization of the electricity grid and promotes the integration of renewable energies.
Frontal shot: RT at sunset in a wide snowy landscape
Longer service intervals
Electric drives require little maintenance. The long service life and high availability of individual components is also reflected in longer service intervals. Electric motors are simpler and more compact. Fewer installed parts mean less vibration. This makes these engines quieter in operation and also contributes to their durability .
Close-up of an electric logo
Sustainability has many faces
Sustainable technology
The simple superstructure of an electric motor compared to conventional motors makes it more efficient. Another advantage of fewer moving parts: the unit is less susceptible to possible functional problems.
RT drives on snow curves at dusk
The strenght is to be found in serenity
Reliable powerhouse
The electric motors accelerate linearly with little energy loss – meaning they transfer power to the road even on steep climbs. Indispensable when every second counts. In addition, the batteries can be used to operate external consumers on site. If the energy supply runs low, the Energy Backup System guarantees smooth process operation drainage .
Two firefighters in GAROS G10 protective suits extinguish a vegetation fire
## Wildfire
Detect. Act. Extinguish.
Two firefighters in contaminated PPE
## Operational hygiene
Stay clean and healthy.
Section of the trend map
## Research & Innovation
Rosenbauer conceives the future - today.

BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT AND THE ECONOMIC SITUATION 1.1. Economic background Up until the first quarter of 2026, the global economy was experiencing an upturn that, whilst not particularly dynamic, was nonetheless robust. The AI-driven technology boom more than offset the dampening effect of the more restrictive US tariff policy; inflation rates were well on the way back to the central banks’ targets, and the central banks were able to ease their monetary policy slightly once again. The outbreak of war in the Middle East and the resulting surge in crude oil prices brought these positive trends to an abrupt halt. Subsequently, economic growth forecasts were revised downwards on several occasions, whilst inflation forecasts were revised upwards – in many cases significantly. The uncertainty surround-ing the duration of the situation and whether it would escalate further or stabilise was so great that economic research institutes began – in addition to their usual practice of presenting a medium-range baseline scenario – to set out several models with considerable ranges in terms of GDP growth and inflation. The baseline scenario was, for the most part, the one that assumed a peace agreement would be reached in the near future, the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened swiftly, and this would lead to a return to more moderate prices and an adequate supply of crude oil and petroleum products. With concrete peace negotiations between the US and Iran having begun in mid-June 2026, this baseline scenario therefore appears to be coming to fruition. Crude oil price volatility is back under control for the time being, uncertainties have eased somewhat, long-term damage is within manageable limits, and it is therefore becoming increasingly likely that the eco-nomic forecasts drawn up on the basis of these assumptions will be borne out. Nevertheless, the sharp downturn in the spring of 2026 marks a turning point in the overall trend: according to the OECD’s forecast of early June 2026, global economic growth for 2026 as a whole is expected to be just 2.8%, down from 3.4% the previous year. Despite the significant rise in global uncertainty and the general sharp increase in the price of crude oil following the outbreak of the war in Iran, economies were affected to varying degrees by the negative consequences. Whilst the impact on the countries in the Middle East directly affected by the conflict was considerable, simply due to the damage caused by the war, many emerging economies in Asia and Latin America appeared relatively unscathed. In the US, the economic slowdown was once again significantly less severe than in Europe. At the turn of the year 2025/26, GDP growth forecasts for the US for the current year 2026 stood at around 2%, whilst inflation forecasts for 2026 were just under 3%. In the case of the former, there were hardly any changes; they remained at around 2% both before the outbreak of the war and after peace negotiations began. Inflation forecasts, on the other hand, were also revised significantly upwards for the US following the outbreak of the war, in some cases by just under 1 percentage point. This has put expectations regarding key interest rates for 2026 into perspective: rather than expecting rate cuts, the consensus is now that policy will remain slightly restrictive for the time being, meaning that key interest rates will stay unchanged. The reason why the Iran conflict has had little impact on the overall US economic momentum is that growth continues to be driven primarily by the AI boom and the associated positive spill-over effects on other sectors. Once again, Europe was particularly vulnerable to headwinds. The GDP growth forecasts for 2026, published in December 2025, were revised downwards from just over 1% for the eurozone as a whole to below 1% during the first half of the year. Inflation forecasts, which at the start of 2026 were still just under 2% for the current year, jumped to around 3%. In order to take decisive action against the marked rise in inflationary pressures, as well as to counter second-round effects and the unanchoring of inflation expectations, the ECB sent a clear signal of its commitment to price stability in mid-June by raising key interest rates by 25 basis points. According to the ECB committee, the decision on whether further rate rises are necessary will be based on the available data. In Austria, as in many economies, the economic impact of the war in the Middle East is still being felt. Assuming that the peace negotiations between the US and Iran are successful, that the Strait of Hormuz remains permanently and fully open, and that crude oil prices do not spike again, the cautious recovery of the Austrian economy, which has been underway since the fourth quarter of 2024, should subsequently regain some momentum following a temporary stagnation in the second and third quarters of 2026. In particular, inflation – which rose sharply following the outbreak of the Iran War – weighed on consumer and business sentiment in the spring. In the manufacturing sector, however, sentiment remained better than it had been a year earlier. This has been facilitated by the fact that more moderate wage agreements have helped to stabilise the competitiveness of Austria’s export-oriented industry to some extent. In this respect, Austria now stands out clearly from Germany and, as things stand, will be well placed to benefit from the expected upturn in the global economy, a trend which is also being underpinned by buoyant demand for investment in equipment and other assets – demand which was only briefly dampened by the Middle East conflict. The downside of falling net real wages is the strain this places on the purchasing power of private households. Consumer demand, which has been weak for some time, nevertheless has the potential to gain momentum: if consumer confidence Interim Financial Report 2026 8 The Group Interim Financial Report 2026 | Business development and the economic situation 8 improves – for example, due to fewer pieces of bad news on the geopolitical front, falling inflation rates, etc. – people might start dipping into their savings and the very high savings rate could be reduced slightly once again. Another cause for concern is the performance of the construction sector, which is set to record its eighth consecutive year of recession this year. The sustained decline in value added – which is particularly pronounced in the building construction sector – carries the risk of a significant and long-term shortage of housing and, consequently, rising prices in this sector. With slightly negative economic growth of around 0.1 per cent, Upper Austria was among the federal states with the weakest growth momentum in 2025. This was largely due to the marked weakness of the export-oriented industry, which is now gradually regaining its footing but remains vulnerable to international risks. As is the case for Austria as a whole, Upper Austria also has considerable potential for further growth in consumer spending. The construction sector is likely to remain in recession in Upper Austria this year as well. Overall, Upper Austria is expected to achieve economic growth in 2026 of just under 1%, in line with the national average. 1.2. Business development On the basis of its forward-looking, sustainable and future-oriented strategy, Raiffeisenlandesbank Oberösterreich man-aged to continue its successful course in the first six months of 2026 as well. The interim results underscore the strength of its business model and demonstrate that Raiffeisenlandesbank Oberösterreich is not only pursuing long-term prospects for the future but also providing effective responses to current economic and geopolitical challenges. The successful business performance of Raiffeisenlandesbank Oberösterreich is particularly noticeable in the financing volume (loans and advances to customers), which stands at EUR 26.5 billion as at 30 June 2026, representing slight growth of 3.0% compared to the end of 2025.
